review_notes: Read the whole file and FaceCombinations.lean's mem_of_pos_of_eq_convexCombination signature. The main duplication is the "split off the positive-weight term, normalize the remainder, and use extremality" argument. It is proved twice, once for indexed families (lines ~84-143) and again for VertexWeights (lines ~200-276). Separately, the attach/subtype reindexing is written out inline in mem_face_of_pos. I did not compile the proposed replacement, so exact tactic details (e.g. the Finset.sum_coe_sort / sum_attach rewriting, and instance ordering for Fintype of the subtype) are uncertain. The mathematical content follows from the signatures read.

findings.problem: This proof re-derives, over a Finset-indexed weight function, exactly the argument already proved in `eq_of_pos_of_eq_convexCombination_of_mem_vertexSet` earlier in the same file: isolate the positive-weight term, set c to the sum of the remaining weights, normalize them by c⁻¹, show the normalized combination lies in the convex set or hull and exhibit q in a segment or the hull of the complement of {q}, then contradict extremality. The two blocks are roughly 60 and 75 lines of nontrivial reasoning (the erase/sum_erase_add bookkeeping, hbaryErase, the normalized nonnegativity/sum/barycenter facts, and the extremality contradiction). The indexed lemma's conclusion `points i = q` under `hq : q ∈ P.vertexSet` is precisely this theorem's statement once the family is the vertex finset. A fix to the extremality step would currently have to be made in both places. The attach-reindexing needed to specialise the indexed lemma is also already written inline in `mem_face_of_pos` (lines 174-197), so that boilerplate would be duplicated a second time if this theorem used the indexed lemma without a shared helper.
findings.proposed_change: Add one helper that turns `W : P.VertexWeights q` into indexed data over the subtype `{x // x ∈ P.vertexFinset}`. For example, `theorem VertexWeights.sum_subtype_weight : ∑ i : {x // x ∈ P.vertexFinset}, W.weight i.1 = 1` and `theorem VertexWeights.sum_subtype_weight_smul : q = ∑ i : {x // x ∈ P.vertexFinset}, W.weight i.1 • i.1`. Proof sketch: `Finset.sum_coe_sort` or `← Finset.attach_eq_univ` followed by `Finset.sum_attach`, then `W.sum_eq_one` and `W.weighted_sum_eq`. Then reprove `eq_of_pos_of_mem_vertexSet` as `eq_of_pos_of_eq_convexCombination_of_mem_vertexSet (fun i : {x // x ∈ P.vertexFinset} ↦ i.1) (fun i ↦ W.weight i.1) q (fun i ↦ P.vertexFinset_subset_carrier i.2) (fun i ↦ W.nonnegative i.1 i.2) W.sum_subtype_weight W.sum_subtype_weight_smul hq (i := ⟨v, hv⟩) hpos`, which gives `v = q` directly. The ~75-line by_contra proof disappears. Reprove `mem_face_of_pos` with the same two helper lemmas, replacing its two inline calc blocks. The helpers need only the existing imports.
findings.benefit: This removes about 75 lines of duplicated convex-combination and extremality reasoning, so the key step is maintained in one place. The Finset-to-subtype reindexing is then also stated once and used by both `mem_face_of_pos` and `eq_of_pos_of_mem_vertexSet`. `weight_eq_zero_of_mem_vertexSet_of_ne` is unaffected because it only uses the statement.
